summary: The article provides a generally accurate and comprehensive overview of market makers in the Indian stock market, their functions, and regulatory aspects.

claims.claim: In India, Market Makers are regulated by SEBI and the stock exchanges.
claims.note: SEBI and stock exchanges (like NSE and BSE) regulate market makers in India.

claims.claim: A Market Maker continuously displays two prices for a share: a bid price (the price at which they are willing to buy the shares from you) and an ask price (the price at which they are willing to sell the shares to you).
claims.note: Market makers continuously quote both bid (buy) and ask (sell) prices.

claims.claim: In India, typically, financial institutions like brokerage firms, banks, or dedicated trading firms with sufficient capital and technological infrastructure can be approved as Market Makers by the stock exchanges and SEBI.
claims.note: Brokerage firms, merchant bankers, and financial institutions can act as market makers in India, registered with SEBI and stock exchanges.

claims.claim: The Market Maker shall be required to provide a 2-way quote for 75% of the time in a day.
claims.note: Market makers are required to provide a two-way quote for 75% of the trading day.

claims.claim: There would not be more than five Market Makers per scrip.
claims.note: There should not be more than five Market Makers for any SME company.

claims.claim: Market making is mandatory for 3 years from the date of listing.
claims.note: Market making is mandatory for a minimum of three years from the date of listing on SME platforms.

claims.claim: Must hold a minimum net worth of ₹1 crore (tiered upward for market makers managing multiple companies)
claims.note: A market maker must hold a minimum net worth of ₹1 crore, with tiered increases for managing multiple companies.

article_title: Who Keeps Our Stock Market Running Smoothly? Understanding Market Makers
